Ava (Acme): Hey team — we're seeing users who should have been deprovisioned still listed as active and with the CustomerAdmin role. This started after we removed groups in Okta last night. Can you help?
Priya (CS): Sorry — can you paste one example user id and the Okta group id you removed?
Ava (Acme): user: acme|u-8242, okta_group: 00g7abcdEFGH. Here is the audit note from Okta: 'Group deleted 2026-03-16T22:03:12Z'.
Priya (CS): Thanks. I'm seeing SCIM PATCHes failing for that org around the same time with 403 from our token validation service. Will fetch logs.
scim-sync-bot: [log] 2026-03-16T22:03:13Z connector=okta org=acme event=group_delete scim_payload={"operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"members[value eq \"00g7abcdEFGH\"]"}]} status=queued
OpsBot: incident-create: created #inc-8242 for "ACME SCIM deprovision mismatch"
Jared (Eng): Looking at the connector logs: 403 responses with text "token scope insufficient: scim.groups.write required". But the account is on Dedicated and we rotated the Okta token last week.
Ava (Acme): We didn't change scopes for the token. Okta says the API token has full SCIM scopes.
Priya (CS): Can you paste the exact error we got downstream?
scim-sync-bot: [log] 2026-03-16T22:03:13Z scim.request id=req-9c4 status=403 body={"error":"insufficient_scope","error_description":"Token missing: scim.groups.write"}
Jared (Eng): Huh — our token introspection shows scope string "scim.users.write scim.read" (missing scim.groups.write). Looks like token used by the connector is the older one without group scopes. The connector rotated to the new token but the sync worker still cached the old secret.
Elena (Product): Could that explain the role not being removed? If group deletion didn't propagate, role mapping would stay.
Jared (Eng): Exactly. The flow: Okta group removed -> connector sends SCIM PATCH to remove membership -> our service rejects due to scope -> we never reconcile and role mapping stays. Also I see some member entries with externalId having trailing whitespace, so even when PATCH eventually applied, mapping misses match. Example in DB: external_id="00g7abcdEFGH \" (note trailing space).
Priya (CS): Repro steps for us to validate: 1) Force sync for org acme (admin UI). 2) Observe connector used token and introspect token scopes. 3) Try a manual SCIM PATCH to remove the member and check response. 4) If 403, rotate token in our connector and restart worker.
Ava (Acme): We're ready for step 1. Please advise on ETA.
Jared (Eng): ETA ~30m for rotation and restart if ops approves. Short-term workaround: run a backfill job to remove role assignments for users with missing groups. I'll prepare a script.
Priya (CS): Also note: we've seen a handful of other orgs with the same symptom when tokens rotated mid-window — added a pager rule.
Ava (Acme): If you backfill, please include audit info so we can show our auditors.
Jared (Eng): Will do. Sample manual SCIM PATCH we used to repro: 
```\nPATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00g7abcdEFGH
Content-Type: application/json

{ "Operations": [ { "op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"acme|u-8242\"]" } ] }
```
Response when using bad token: 
```\nHTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ "error": "insufficient_scope", "error_description": "Token missing: scim.groups.write" }
```
When using rotated token: 
```\nHTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```
Elena (Product): Root cause hypothesis: connector rotated to a new token but some long-lived sync workers cached the previous token. Secondary issue: group externalId normalization (trailing spaces/case) causes mismatch during role->group reconciliation. Fixes: 1) Immediate: rotate token and restart sync workers + run backfill job. 2) Medium: add token rotation signal to workers to invalidate caches. 3) Longer: normalization layer for externalId (trim, lowercase) and add a migration to normalize stored ids.
Priya (CS): I'll run the forced sync and coordinate with ops. Ava — we'll share step-by-step and once backfill completes, send audit CSV.
Ava (Acme): Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.
Priya (CS): Follow-up: ops rotated token and restarted workers. After restart manual PATCHs succeeded. Backfill job started and removed 12 role links. Scheduled a follow-up tomorrow to confirm no drift. :thumbsup:
